accuracy: Typical accuracy ±5–10 °C absolute; better for ranking configurations than for absolute temperatures.
scope: Air-cooled only. GPU water blocks are out of scope.

The right fan pulls air through the finstack ... exhausted right out the other side of the card" (https://www.tomshardware.com/news/a-closer-look-at-the-geforce-rtx-3080-rtx-3090-founders-edition-coolers). Gamers Nexus: about 72 °C at steady state with 21–22 °C ambient, fans about 1570 RPM, memory 89–90 °C. Tom's Hardware (https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/nvidia-geforce-rtx-5090-review/8): ~80 °C in Cyberpunk at 572 W, GDDR7 96 °C. The open-air target used here is about 76 °C at 25 °C ambient, between the two. Fan intercepts, fin geometry and TIM are in gpusim/calib.py.

NVIDIA's datasheet says thermal solution 'Active' and does not publish a P–Q curve. The blower description (enclosed shroud, rear-bracket exhaust) is from board-partner and retailer writeups such as https://www.centralcomputer.com/blog/post/understanding-the-nvidia-rtx-6000-pro-blackwell-lineup-workstation-max-q-and-server-editions. Blower free air, dead-head pressure, fin geometry and TIM live in gpusim/calib.py and are joint-fit to open air plus anchors A and B.

cards.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (600 W)
cards.notes: Datasheet: total board power 600 W; 5.4" H × 12" L, dual slot, extended height; thermal solution "Double-flow-through". Two axial fans in a housing nearly identical to the RTX 5090 FE (https://www.pugetsystems.com/labs/articles/nvidia-rtx-pro-6000-blackwell-workstation-content-creation-review/). AEC Magazine: it "draws air in from beneath the card and vents it out of the top ... hot air from one card can be pulled straight into the next" (https://aecmag.com/workstations/review-nvidia-rtx-pro-blackwell-series-gpus/). No published sustained-load die temperature was found. The open-air target is the 5090 FE review figure plus the extra 25 W, and is approximate. Fan intercepts, fin geometry and TIM are in gpusim/calib.py.

cases.name: Corsair iCUE LINK 9000D RGB AIRFLOW
cases.notes: Real case. The Mike Bradley build that uses it is a separate illustrative mock.
cases.dimension_note: Corsair lists height 698 mm, length 698 mm, width 307 mm. Expansion: '8 Horizontal (or 4 Vertical) + 2 Vertical (For Secondary Motherboard)'. Modelled here as 8 horizontal + 2 vertical. Front/top 140 mm and 120 mm patterns are alternate InfiniRail layouts. Rev 4 models the front as the 8×120 pattern, 4 high × 2 wide (Corsair: "dual 480mm radiators side-by-side"), and the rear as 1×140 (Corsair: rear 2×120 or 1×140), and the top as one row of 4×120 by default, with the full 8×120 grid (2 wide × 4 deep, Corsair: top 8×120) as the `8x120` pattern. Bottom has no fan or radiator support. PSU max length 225 mm. The rear 2×120 option is modelled as two fans stacked vertically above the slots, next to the CPU cooler (as in Mike Bradley's build photos, per Stefano). Corsair lists "Included Fans: No Fans Included"; the 9000D template populates the front array with AF120 RGB ELITE as an assumption. The two extra vertical slots are, per Corsair, for a secondary motherboard; the model uses them as vertical GPU positions for convenience.

builds.name: Stefano's Meshify 2 XL — 4× RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q
builds.notes: Fan layout confirmed by Stefano (2026-09-28): 3× redux-1700 front intake, one redux-1700 intake on the top at the front, one on the bottom at the front, the Arctic 360 slid to the rear of the top as exhaust, one rear exhaust, and the rear GPU shroud with its two iPPC-3000 fans side by side. Anchor A is this layout with the shroud off. The factorial stock cell is stacked (no empty slot), shroud off, standard pressure, leaky — it is not this saved build. Front 3× Noctua 140 mm redux-1700 intake, rear 1× redux-1700 exhaust, Arctic 360 on top as exhaust with its three P12 fans. Bottom mounts are blanked. All PCIe slot brackets removed. Rear shroud with 2× NF-A14 industrialPPC-3000 is fitted (shroud mode on). GPU fan curve is stock. scenarios.title: Mike Bradley's Dengen X Station
scenarios.disclaimer: Modelled from Mike Bradley's public posts. His measured numbers: bottom 49 °C, top 79 °C at ~80 % fans; top 69 °C at 100 %.

steps.title: As built — four Workstation cards touching, 275 W, fans ~80 %
talking_points: Four RTX PRO 6000 Workstation cards, no gap between them, capped at 275 W.
These cards pull air from underneath and blow it out of the top, so the stack is four fans in series. Each card breathes the one below it; the top card sees the hottest air.
Model about 47 → 79 °C bottom to top. His posted numbers are 49 → 79 °C.

steps.title: GPU fans at 100 %
talking_points: Same stack, fans pinned to 100 %. More air through the column, less rise per card.
Model about 45 → 70 °C. He posted 49 → 69 °C.

steps.title: Full 600 W per card, fans 100 %
talking_points: Lift the cap to the full 600 W. The heat per card more than doubles; the column cannot carry it, and the upper cards reach the 90 °C cutoff and throttle.
This is why he runs the stack at 275 W.

scenarios.title: Rear shroud A/B — open plenum vs taped stack
scenarios.disclaimer: Predicted, ahead of the live test. Orientation A is the printed shroud on the gapped Meshify. Orientation B stacks the four cards and tapes the shroud down to the GPU exhaust openings. Absolute temperatures are ±5–10 °C; the ranking is what the hardware A/B should check.

steps.title: A — printed shroud, open plenum
talking_points: Slots 1/4/7 plus vertical v2, shroud on. Hottest die 84.5 °C. Dies 84.4, 84.4, 84.4, 84.5 °C. Memory 83.2, 83.1, 83.1, 83.3 °C. Exhaust 44.9, 44.8, 44.8, 44.9 °C. Through-GPU 26.0 CFM on every card.

The two interior gaps bypass 23 CFM each (46 CFM together) into the plenum at about −28 Pa. The four GPU mouths carry about 28 CFM of hot exhaust each. The shroud does not pull the top of the top card, the bottom of the bottom card, or either face of the vertical card.
Skin convection uses that bypass, about 5.4 W/m²K, roughly 7 W on an end card and 14 W on the middle card. It does not use the fin flow.

steps.title: B — stacked and taped to the GPU mouths
talking_points: Four cards in slots 1/3/5/7, gaps taped. Hottest unthrottled die 103.7 °C on the second card; the stack throttles near 89.5 °C. Unthrottled dies 96.6, 103.7, 103.0, 85.1 °C. Memory 95.4, 102.5, 101.8, 83.8 °C. Exhaust 53.0, 57.8, 57.5, 44.9 °C.

Through-GPU flow 18.9, 15.7, 15.7, 26.8 CFM. The middle cards are inlet-starved across 3.6 mm, so they move less air than in A even though the plenum is pulled to about −65 Pa. Crack flow is 0.9 CFM per gap, 2.7 CFM total, against about 84 CFM through the exhaust openings.

At the same gap1 spacing, tape alone raises through-GPU flow from 26.0 to 26.9 CFM and cuts the bypass from 46 CFM to a 1.6 CFM crack (plenum −28 Pa to −50 Pa). Stacking, not the tape, is what makes B hotter. Facing skins exchange a few watts by conduction and radiation; h there is about 2.1 W/m²K.

steps.title: Close-packed, no shroud (anchor B)
talking_points: Four dual-slot blowers in adjacent slots. The fan face points down, so each card inhales the gap below it, only about 3.6 mm between cards. The bottom card's fan faces the PSU-shroud clearance instead.
The stock blower curve is already at its ~70 % duty cap, so the cards cannot spin harder as they heat up.
Unthrottled dies are about 101, 109, 109 and 87 °C, top to bottom, the middle two near 15 CFM. Three cards cross 90 °C and throttle to the cutoff.

steps.title: Gaps plus a vertical card, shroud off (anchor A)
talking_points: One empty slot between horizontal cards, brackets removed, so the downward fan face sees an open slot instead of the next card's backplate.
The fourth card moves to a vertical slot off to the side.
Hottest die 86.6 °C, all four within 0.1 °C, about 26 CFM each. Nothing throttles. This is the measured anchor.

steps.title: Rear shroud with 2× NF-A14 iPPC-3000
talking_points: The shroud is a shared plenum over every bracket. Two industrial 140s pull on it. Interior gaps between the cards are their own orifices into that plenum, in parallel with the GPU exhaust openings. The top of the top card and the bottom of the bottom card are not inlets.

Hottest die 84.5 °C. Mean blower flow rises from 25.8 to 26.0 CFM. About 46 CFM bypasses through the two gaps and cools the skins; it does not go through the fins. The plenum stops plume re-ingestion through the open slot mouths.

steps.title: Positive pressure, interfaces taped
talking_points: Every case fan and the radiator flip to intake. Seals go to level 4–5 (tape).
Case pressure goes to about +18 Pa, which cuts recirculation, but the radiator now heats the intake with the CPU. Hottest die 85.5 °C, slightly worse than 84.2.

steps.title: Custom Accelerated GPU fan curve
talking_points: Custom Accelerated is off at 25 °C and ramps linearly to 100 % at 70 °C, instead of capping near 70 % duty.
Affinity laws: flow scales with RPM, pressure with RPM squared. Hottest die 75.4 °C, about 37 CFM. One card in open air: 73.4 °C on this curve against 82.8 °C stock.

steps.title: Same slots, 4× RTX PRO 6000 Workstation (600 W flow-through)
talking_points: The Workstation Edition draws air in from beneath and vents it out of the top. With one empty slot (about 21 mm) the card above breathes half of that exhaust.
Unthrottled dies about 95, 93 and 83 °C top to bottom, 83 °C on the vertical card. The top two throttle. Open the network view to see the plume branches.
The shroud barely matters here; most of the heat now leaves through the case fans, not the rear brackets.

steps.title: Optimal air-cooled search
talking_points: The optimizer searches fan direction, shroud, spacing and the GPU fan curve on the same solver. Water blocks are not in the search.
Treat the winner as the next thing to try on the real machine, not as a guaranteed temperature.
